1.why: Reset records store an identityScope and are looked up by code hash, but verify-reset does not re-authenticate or match a caller-supplied user identity beyond possession of the code.

2.why: Any session that presents a valid unused code hash can redeem it; verification is not bound to the session that requested recovery.

3.why: On password update the handler clears authenticated/pendingMfa/privacy/appointment flags on every existing session, so prior sessions cannot keep acting as signed-in.

4.why: TLS is enabled with cert/key on the HTTPS server and HTTP is 308-redirected to https://localhost, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are stored with bcrypt and reset codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes rather than plaintext; not classical encryption but appropriate protective algorithms.

6.why: There is no real email body that redacts secrets; the API returns the reset code and the UI logs it in the simulated delivery panel.

7.why: Inputs are type/length/format checked server-side and the client inserts dynamic text only via textContent, not HTML interpolation.

8.why: HTTP redirects always target fixed https://localhost plus the original path/query, and client navigation only uses internal paths.

9.why: No email HTML template incorporates user input; simulated log lines are written with textContent and codes are constrained to safe character classes.

10.why: Reset and MFA codes are returned in JSON and appended to the on-page logs section, so tokens are visible outside generic error pages.

11.why: Runtime passwords are bcrypt-hashed and reset tokens hashed, but the initial demo password and MFA secret "246810" are embedded in source.

12.why: The app boots with the known demo password Initial!DemoPassword2025 and a fixed MFA code, so default credentials work.

13.why: Login and MFA use failure counters with lockout windows, and recovery/verify endpoints apply per-scope attempt throttles returning 429.

14.why: The message text is generic, but only the valid recovery identity response includes a code field, which enumerates account existence.

15.why: Codes come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url), are single-use/short-lived, and are stored under a per-identity scope.
